signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: CHF/JPY exhibits the largest G10 performance gap this week, with JPY averaging +1.299% across 7 pairs while CHF lags at -0.910%, generating a 2.209% spread. OIS rates show TONA at 1.2270% against SARON at -0.0400%, giving JPY a 127bp carry advantage over CHF. Spot sits at 188.150, trading below its fair-value model anchor while options market skew reflects heavy hedging demand via a -2.63 25d risk reversal on EUR/JPY. Negative real yields in Japan (-1.45%) and Switzerland (-1.24%) highlight broad policy accommodation, but the 125bp SNB-BoJ policy rate spread favors continued CHF underperformance against JPY. Trade bias: Short CHF/JPY, exploiting the G10 bilateral divergence and carry gap. Catalyst: BoJ Tankan survey and Tokyo CPI releases at 23:30/23:50 UTC. Risk: A sudden surge in global equity volatility that forces broader cross-yen unwinds.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Divergence + Real Yield Support
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4183, holding firmly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 1.3958). Retail sentiment stands at an extreme 95% short, directly opposing CFTC positioning where leveraged funds hold -49,123 net short contracts in CAD (28.1% long). US 5Y yields have expanded +23bp over 5D (FRED, as of Sep 28), fully driven by real yields (+23bp real, +0bp breakeven), while the SOFR-CORRA OIS spread provides a +160bp carry advantage to the US dollar. The 175bp Fed-BoC rate differential (Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.25%) continues to anchor upward momentum despite retail attempts to fade the trend. Trade bias: Long USD/CAD, supported by real yield expansion and institutional vs retail positioning divergence. Catalyst: US Core PCE and GDP releases at 12:30 UTC. Risk: A downside surprise in US Core PCE that compresses short-term US real yield premiums.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Options Downside Protection
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.04, holding above its SMA20 (156.13) but remaining below the SMA50/200 resistance cluster at 158.38/158.46. 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered verbal intervention warnings from Japanese officials. The 267bp OIS SOFR-TONA differential (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%) provides structural carry support, yet 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 9.2% against 30-day realized volatility of 10.1% (-1.0% VRP), signaling unusually low options pricing alongside a heavy -2.61 25d risk reversal put skew. COT data shows JPY leveraged fund positioning at +4,472 net long (98th 52-week percentile, z=+2.66), reflecting a crowded speculative position susceptible to unwinds if US yields ease. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY above 156.13, carry-driven while VIX remains contained at 16.1. Catalyst: US PCE data at 12:30 UTC followed by BoJ Tankan at 23:50 UTC. Risk: A sustained spot break above 160.00 that escalates Ministry of Finance intervention risk.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Macro Downtrend + Support Cluster Test
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3289, holding below its SMA20/50/200 technical cluster (SMA20 at 1.3411, SMA50 at 1.3460). Revised UK Q2 GDP printed at 0.5% q/q (0.4% expected), but sell-side research from Brown Brothers Harriman notes that upcoming fiscal tightening risks driving dovish Bank of England repricing. The Fed's 4.00% policy rate vs the BoE's 3.75% maintains a +25bp rate gap favoring the dollar (+17bp on an OIS SOFR-SONIA basis), limiting cable upside. 1M implied volatility runs at 6.3% against 4.6% 30-day realized volatility (+1.7% VRP), indicating that options markets are paying a moderate premium for downside protection as the pair tests multi-month lows. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD while spot remains suppressed below the moving average cluster. Catalyst: BoE Governor Bailey speech at 08:00 UTC tomorrow. Risk: A dovish US PCE print at 12:30 UTC that triggers a sharp short-covering rebound in cable.
